title: HER SISTER WAS LOVED MORE.
paragraphs: HER SISTER WAS LOVED MORE.
Leah knew it.

Every glance from Jacob went past her…
…straight to Rachel.

The silence at the dinner table.
The cold space in the marriage bed.
The quiet ache of being the second choice.

Unloved.
Overlooked.
Forgotten.
But Scripture whispers something powerful.
“When the LORD saw that Leah was hated, He opened her womb…” — Book of Genesis 29:31
God saw Leah.

Not the beautiful sister everyone praised.
Not the woman Jacob adored.
Leah.
The one nobody celebrated.
And from Leah’s pain, God began writing redemption.

Her sons were born one by one—
Reuben.
Simeon.
Levi.
Each name carried the cry of her heart:
“Maybe now my husband will love me.”
But the fourth son… something changed.
She stopped chasing Jacob’s love.
She lifted her eyes to heaven and said:
“This time I will praise the LORD.”
And she named the child Judah.

From Judah would come the royal line.
From Judah would come the Lion.
From Judah would come Jesus Christ.
The Savior of the world was born from the womb of the woman who felt unloved.
Let that sink in.
God built the road to the Cross through the tears of an overlooked woman.

So if you feel invisible today…
If someone else seems more loved, more chosen, more celebrated…
Hear this truth:
He sees you.
The same God who saw Leah sees your quiet suffering, your hidden prayers, your late-night tears.
And in Christ, your story is never wasted.
What feels like rejection may be the beginning of redemption.
Because with Jesus—
the overlooked become chosen.
Have you ever felt overlooked… like someone else was loved more?
Tell me your story. Let’s bring it into the light.
